title: Ingest shunt + session coalescer to reduce tokenization overhead for short prompts
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Background: We see disproportionate CPU and latency overhead on the prefill (ingest) side for short, high-QPS prompts (e.g., chat pings, single-line completions). Tokenization/normalization and session-level KV init account for >35% of tail latency for these requests in our Canary traces. Goal: reduce per-request prefill latency and CPU for short prompts (<= 64 tokens) without harming long-sequence throughput or correctness. Deliver a production-tested ingestion fast-path (shunt) plus a session coalescer that safely batches or deduplicates tokenization work across concurrent requests from the same session or client.
acceptance_criteria: P95 prefill latency for short prompts reduced by >= 30% in our benchmark cluster (p95 measured across 10k samples)
Tokenization CPU cycles per short request reduced by >= 25% under synthetic QPS 2500 test
No regression on existing decode throughput (<= 3% variance) for long sequences
Fallback correctness: shunt + coalescer produce identical token sequences vs canonical pipeline for UTF-8 inputs; differential tests included
Feature gated and togglable via runtime flag and console rollout controls
implementation_plan: 1) Add a lightweight ASCII/UTF8 classifier (shunt) in the ingress lane to detect fast-pathable inputs. The classifier must be O(n) single-pass and avoid allocations when possible.

2) Implement a session coalescer that groups simultaneous short-prompt tokenization requests from the same session/client for up to 10-20ms; coalescer returns shared tokenization outcome where prompts share identical normalized prefix fingerprint.

3) Introduce an in-memory session-level ingest cache with small fixed-size entries (fingerprint -> token slice) and TTL=60s, LRU eviction. Cache keys are content-addressed (sha1 of normalized text + model id + tokenizer_version).
4) Extend kernel-selection hints API: post a short-prompt hint to the scheduler (expected_output_len_estimate < 64) so decode workers can pick reduced-KV warmup kernels and smaller batching windows.
5) Add attention-optimizer flag: for single-turn requests, skip full multi-head KV allocation until decode step is reached; pre-allocate a minimal header to avoid double-copy.
6) Integrate canary telemetry: tokenization-hit-rate, coalescer-latency, any-fallback-rate, and end-to-end p95. Instrument with existing tracer tags so Console can show per-route breakdown.
7) Run A/B in Canary fleet with gradual rollout and kill-switch. Validate with regression evals and fuzzed unicode corpus.
8) Post-mortem and tunings: after 1 week of traffic, adjust coalescer window and cache TTL based on real-world hit/cost trade-off.
notes: Trade-offs: coalescing introduces a small added delay (10-20ms) for first request; this must be balanced vs throughput CPU savings. We'll gate by route and request size thresholds.
Security: caching keys must not include PII. Normalization step will canonicalize and redact ephemeral tokens if route policy requires it. Security review flagged but no HSM/KMS changes needed.
Compatibility: tokenizer_version must be part of cache key so rollout of tokenizer changes won't serve stale tokens. We'll increment version in deploys and evict relevant entries.
Related work: kernel hinting will interact with runtime's batch scheduler; coordinate with scheduling folks to ensure hint paths don't starve larger batches.
